Ah, a fellow traveler from Veloth. I feasted there, once, on the thought-books of the wizards of the extreme east. I sapped their energy and stole their sanity and grew bloated on their knowledge, until imprisoned here. If you can get here, then I can leave.

Sotha Sil is decrepit and in ruins. Its destruction broke my seal, and now I plan to leave. But you are, of course, a tiresome hero, intent on my destruction. Vehk himself could only contain me. So how do you plan to do away with the Pocket Cabal? Might or magic? I won't even consider the possibility of guile.

Of course a fool like you would try to use brute force. It's worked for all your problems so far, hasn't it? You just hit things until they stop moving. I am afraid you'll find, however, that there's nothing here to hit.
Magic? I knew you were stupid, but I never guessed the sheer depths of your idiocy. I AM magic! The spell-twister itself, all the secrets of the Psijics embodied! By all means, try a spell.

Ah, Illusion, one of the most subtle schools. It changes perception, not reality, you will never be able to change what is or is not, only what seems to be. But, what if perception IS reality? Why, you could be a god. Something worth pondering.

Destruction. Most mages deride it at a blunt instrument, barely worth consideration at an academic level. Be wary! Destruction begets destruction, and always seeks its own. But under a steady will, a well-aimed bolt may carve a jagged gash through history.

Conjuration is a trap for the careless and the foolish. Creatures bound only work under sufference, and the Daedra are ever eager to betray. They are immortal, and their memories stretch endlessly. If you use wise and courteous, you may survive. Never suppose that any being is completely under your thrall.
Alteration creates no mere change in perception, it affects what is. In many ways, Alteration is the most grounded of the schools of magic. Just remember, grounded isn't the same as simple.
I confess, I never get much of a chance to practice Restoration. I suppose I can always experiment on you, but not even Restoration can bring back the dead.

You cannot explain Mysticism, it defies the hopes of would-be scholars seeking to fit it to a definition. It is a school of paradoxes and internal inconsistencies, and the Psijics treat is at a way of life. Mysticism cannot be taught, and each of us studies it in solitude.

Nerevarine. Here it ends. This Clockwork City was to be your death. You were to be my greatest martyr! The heroic Nerevarine, sacrificing all to protect Morrowind from the mad Sotha Sil. But you live! You live!

Fear not. I will tell the tale myself when this is done. I will tell my people how with your dying breath you proclaimed your devotion to me, the one true god. Your death will end this prophecy and unite my people again under one god, one faith, one rule by my divine law. The puppet king will lay down his arms and bow to my will. Those who do not yield will be destroyed.
The Mazed Band has allowed me to travel to this place. Here, I slew Sotha Sil. Here, I summoned the Fabricants to attack Mournhold. I will be the savior of my people! I alone will be their salvation!

But I smell the blood of gods on your hands, Nerevarine. Vivec was a fool. I'm sorry I wasn't there to see his death. But Sotha Sil...he always thought himself our better, shunning us, locking himself in this hole. He spoke not a word as he died. Not a whisper. Even in death, he mocked me with his silence! But I think you will scream, mortal. For now, you face the one true god.

None may stand in my way. Not you, and certainly not Vivec. He is a poet, a fool. I will deal with him when I have finished with you. And Sotha Sil...he always thought himself our better, shunning us, locking himself in this hole. He spoke not a word as he died. Not a whisper. Even in death, he mocked me with his silence! It is almost impossible to describe what happens next, but you try. Knowledge flows through your brain almost like water through a strainer, leaving behind tidbits. You know more, you have done more. Time is nothing, time is everything. Your eyes burn, and you drop the scroll, which closers. You feel like somehow you have gained a small bit of... something.

So. You've made it here, and have slain my mad sister. Are you surprised to find my lifeless corpse, mortal? Or, should I say, hero? She murdered me long before you arrived, thanks to the power of the Mazed Band. But, despite my death, I am Sotha Sil, and his city, and all that you have seen.

This is my realm, and though she destroyed my corporeal shell, I remain alive within the walls, gears, and circuits of this city, though the transferal was hasty and imperfect. This is why you needed to act as my hands. Now, you have a choice, mortal.

Will you aid me one last time, and complete the process to merge me fully and perfectly with my realm, or will you slay me as well, as veangence for your predecesor? You would be well within your rights to, and I bear no ill-will should you choose to do so. Just be aware that, as I die, so too shall my city, in time, a corpse of a corpse, a dead god's husk drifting through nothing and returning to nothing.
Complete Sotha Sil's upload process, or sever his lifeline, killing him and the city?

I thank you, mortal, though not on my own behalf, but on behalf of my creations and my children living within my city. I grew weary of my own existence, but perhaps, in caring for my people, I shall find some joy again. The city is yours, as well, in all but name, and you may enter and leave at your leisure. I also leave my personal workshop to you, given that I no longer have any need for it, and lack the arms to use it besides.
In return, I have one final request. Should I begin to descend into madness, you must slay me without mercy. This will be a kindness.

So, you've decided to sever my spirit and return me to the Dreaming Sleeve. This is, perhaps, the best decision, and I was growing weary of my existence. I could not say for sure whether or not I would have gone down the path of my once-sister to Sheogorath's domain. You may have just done the world a great kindness, hero, though I mourn for the fate of my creations and my children.
I give you my final gift, to my boon and bane, my workshop. Please treat it kindly, and take care of my city in the few years it has left.
Life and Machine systems repaired, manufactoring plant fully cleansed.

Origin: Alinor. Classificiation: Sentient, Nondangerous. Large scale altmerian crystal voidship, wrong traversal lead to it gaining sentience. Captured by Psijics, transferred to Lord Sotha for safekeeping. Weapons not under control of sentience, low class threat.

Origin: Skyrim. Classification: Alive, endangered. Floating whale-like animal, previously common sight in Skyrim air, 2nd era purges lead to near extinction. Possible breeding program on other planes suggested.

Origin: Vvardenfell. Classification: Sentient, humanoid, dangerous. Believed Sixth House associated, testing shows dunmer originally, current appearance matches no known entity. Possible divine intervention from Sharmat suggested.
Origin: Old Cyrod. Classification: Aquatic, territorial. Large serpent, inhabited Imperial rivers until Red King's intervention. Last known specimen, highly valuable.

Origin: Unknown Classification: Docile, metaphysical. Very large moth species. Friendly, overexposure leads to possible clairvoyance and in extreme cases blindness. Smaller versions commonplace, larger versions dangerous.
